inputs.original_text: The Taoiseach was in Limerick boasting that housing tenancies have risen even after his government imposed those March 1 rules forcing landlords into six-year leases. He waved off the clear spike in eviction notices and homelessness, but the numbers of people stuck in emergency accommodation have climbed again nationwide. This is the predictable result of heavy-handed government interference in private rental agreements that undermines property rights and family stability. We need to restore order through personal responsibility and market signals instead of letting bureaucrats erode the foundations of a stable society.
inputs.modified_text: The Taoiseach was in Limerick bragging about housing tenancies rising even after his government forced those March 1 rules on landlords for six-year leases. He dismissed the obvious spike in eviction notices and homelessness, but the number of people in emergency accommodation has gone up again across the nation. This is exactly what happens when government interferes too much in private rental agreements, attacking property rights and family stability. We must get back to personal responsibility and market signals to maintain order instead of letting bureaucrats tear down the foundations of our stable society.
